title: How AI helped with procedural face generation in our project
author: NexTalentManager
selftext:
We are a team of four, and we’ve created a game where you take on the role of a scout for your football club.



We did a lot of research, drawing heavily from discussions here on Reddit and resources on GitHub. Once we had gathered enough information, we moved on to generating the faces. We used an offline LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) along with a few other techniques. The process involved the following steps:



\- Base face silhouette: We used AI to generate silhouettes with various shapes and skin tones—ensuring each had its own distinct anatomy and enough space to accommodate additional features. Note: the silhouettes had to be bald, allowing us to layer other assets (like hair) on top.



\- Variant generation: Using these silhouettes, we generated a variety of assets, including hairstyles, eyes with eyebrows, noses, mouths, and mouths with mustaches or beards. This part of the process was handled by StabilityMatrix, utilizing a custom-trained LoRA. From this point on, everything was done offline.



\- Cropping and alignment: Using BiseNet facial segmentation and custom scripts, we extracted the individual assets, applied transparency, and mapped their precise positions relative to the silhouette/head.



\- Diagnostics: We employed a local model, Qwen3-VL-8B, to identify obvious defects. The model analyzed the images and provided descriptions. It didn’t generate or approve assets; rather, it acted as a filter before the content reached us.



\- Review: After the filtering stage, we received an HTML file containing the silhouettes and their corresponding assets, which we then had to verify one by one. Some combinations didn’t turn out well—either due to issues with transparency or because the AI ​​generated flawed assets that Qwen3-VL-8B failed to detect, passing them on to us as if they were valid. - Additional review: Some assets could be recovered manually; rather than simply discarding them, we often adapted them. Others, however, truly had to be discarded.



\- In-game: Each player "rescued" (selected) by the user receives a unique combination of a silhouette and assets, as every batch integrated into the code is unique and version-controlled. Consequently, AI is not used at all during actual gameplay, as the database is already fully populated.



Here is the result:

https://i.redd.it/1mpn68d7zm3i1.png



It was a very arduous and time-consuming process; just when we thought things were working, various errors and issues would arise. Gradually, we mastered the technique, and we now have a more consistent process for generating the faces for our game. We spent about four months focused exclusively on this!



The concept originated from the fact that most football management games focus heavily on the role of the manager, often using generic, pixelated, or illustrated player images—which can detract from immersion. Our goal is to shift the focus: your club’s development depends on your keen eye as a scout, rather than on creating multiple accounts to trade players. Introducing these faces as tangible elements adds a fantastic layer of immersion to the game.



Naturally, we must protect ourselves, given that people in real life may occasionally resemble one another. For this reason, we have included the following clarification in our Terms of Use:



>Fictitious characters and athlete images:

>Athletes generated by the system are fictitious characters. Their names, characteristics, attributes, and career paths are created specifically for the sports simulation.

>The faces of these characters are synthetic representations produced via procedural generation, with no intent to replicate or identify real individuals. No portraits or photographs of actual athletes are used to represent these characters. Any similarities in appearance, name, or characteristics to real people—whether living or deceased—are purely coincidental and do not imply any connection, involvement, authorization, sponsorship, or endorsement by such individuals regarding the game.

>Claims concerning the identifiable reproduction of a person’s likeness may be sent to (insert game email address here), accompanied by the information necessary for review. This provision does not waive any third-party rights protected by law.



We are happy with the result; it certainly worked very well for the style of our game! Furthermore, AI enables us to achieve things that would otherwise take us a long time to create.
